chapter: Photographs of the Creole Fiesta and family
title: First ball at the Autocrat Club and the usherettes
summary: The first ball in May 1956, pages, and the usherettes at the third Creole Fiesta.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals

blocks.x: Yeah. I see. This is First Ball Autocrat Club, May 12, 1956.
That's our first ball. Yeah, that ought to be recorded if you want some of the...

First ball at the autocrat, huh? Honey, why don't you go put the light on? That light. Maybe we can see that. Oh, you can see. Maybe we can see that. Yeah. Yeah, that's the first ball. Uh-huh. I try to take time and write, you know, what things are, because for future, you know, people will know what it's for. Uh-huh.
Everybody slips away from you on town.
You can get what things are.

Yes, indeed. So now that's this. Now what's all this? Oh, this is me sitting out here with the little boys, the little pages. Now, this is one I want you to see. Have you ever seen so many girls together at one time? You know, that's a good picture of being so many taken in one. Don't you think so? It really is. Now that's taken at the, at the Birgos Quay. These were the, the, um, the, um, uh, maids. What's the matter? These were the, um, the, um, I call them the girls in waiting at the, they were seating the people, which call them usherettes. Usherettes, that's what they were at Birgos Quay. At Birgos Quay. This is Deborah Brown here. Right here. This is Deborah Brown. This is my Sylvia. This is, where is Lois? It's a little girl, live right across the street. She has three babies now already. Imagine. And, uh, this is Joyce and my granddaughter. This is Lois, you know. And, uh, just think how those children grow. You know, you have them at 16 or 15. Then they go and get married first and, you know, they come along with two, three babies. Yeah. And then, and I show them, they're sitting on me, I had this picture. I said, no, that's history. That is history. You may see, but I won't give it to you. You can see it. What's this? Huh? And that's the Creole girls of the neighborhood. They're just, they're really the neighborhood girls. They're really the neighborhood girls. Let me put this ring on here. I'm going to put it on top of here. Now this is, um, now these are the Creoles. Now what are you thinking of? In the costumes. I see. Are they lovely? They're costume old-fashioned costumes. And where were those pictures made? Those were made at, uh, did I say?
Now they were made in the garden, the Creole Fest.

Third, um, the third Creole Fest. But, um, this was made in Mrs. Um, what's that lady's name back there? On Annette Street. Oh, yeah. This is, um, in her garden. This is the lady's garden. And this is Mrs. Theod, Mrs. Patrick, and Mrs. Um, what's her name back there on Annette Street? I forget her name.
Well, it'll come to you in a minute. Yeah.
Uh-huh. And, uh, this poor lady, she died, huh? Wow. This is, I'll let you know about that, Miss. Uh-huh. This is me when I was fat. Big difference from looking at me now.
You lost 35 pounds. 35 pounds, yes, indeed. Uh-huh.
